sources.entry: Back to Bug - Menu bar replay recorder that saves recent screen activity as video for bug reports. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/skarpovdev/backtobug) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Back to Bug is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that keeps a rolling screen recording and saves the last stretch (default 60 seconds) as an MP4 to attach to bug reports.
summary.what_it_does: Back to Bug records the selected display continuously into an in-memory buffer of encoded H.264 frames. Pressing the global shortcut (⌘⇧B by default) or clicking Save replay in the menu bar writes the recent buffer to an MP4 file in ~/Movies/Back to Bug, or a folder the user chooses. Settings let the user change replay length (5 seconds to 10 minutes), display, quality preset with resolution caps, frame rate (15, 30, or 60 fps), cursor and click highlighting, save location, shortcut, and launch-at-login with automatic recording. Recent replays can be played or revealed in Finder from the panel. The README says processing is local with no accounts, uploads, analytics, or network requests, and the buffer is capped at 512 MiB. Replays contain video only, with no microphone or system audio.
use_cases: attach a screen recording to a bug report
capture steps that led to a bug without reproducing it
record recent screen activity while testing
make a short video replay of a glitch
save the last minute of screen for QA
how_to_run: Download the .dmg from the latest release and drag Back to Bug into Applications
Launch the app; it appears in the macOS menu bar
Click Enable screen recording and allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording
Build from source: git clone the repo, cd backtobug, swift test, bash scripts/build.sh
notable: Rolling buffer keeps the last N seconds in memory so a replay can be saved after the bug happens
Global shortcut (⌘⇧B by default) saves a replay from any app
Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel Macs
Releases from v0.1.2 are Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or newer; the app is macOS only
Screen access is broad, so replays can capture other apps and sensitive content; the README advises checking replays before sharing
Older ad-hoc signed builds may be blocked by Gatekeeper and need manual approval, and permission may need re-granting after switching builds
